thread.title: Tencent Music: Overvalued Compared To Other Streamers - Tencent Music Entertainment Group (NYSE:TME)

author: B&B Market
title: Tencent Music: Overvalued Compared To Other Streamers - Tencent Music Entertainment Group (NYSE:TME)
text:
Tencent Music ( TME ) IPO'd roughly a month ago now at the bottom of its projection price. At the current price, TME is valued at $20 billion. At this valuation, it is difficult to determine if TME is actually overvalued. Compared to other streamers, TME is trading at a premium, but this may be warranted by the size of the company and the projected growth of the industry. On the other hand, the premium may be negated based on a strained market for growth, lack of paying subscribers, and high valuation multiples.
TME data by YCharts
Strong Industry Growth; Strained Domestic MAU Growth The entertainment market within China is still young compared to its western counterparts. According to iResearch , the US recorded music market is 45x larger than that in China. This youthful market is expected to increase four-fold within the next 5 years, totaling more than $32 billion. The company's prospectus points out that other entertainment disciplines (online video and video games) have taken off over the last decade within China and become the largest markets across the globe. Despite this, the music paying ratio was only 3.9% in 2017.
(Source: Company Prospectus)
TME is the largest streaming platform within China, boasting more than 800 million monthly active users (MAUs) across 4 different platforms (QQ Music, Kugou, Kuwa, WeSing). This user base cannot be found anywhere else in the industry, and is just the domestic base for TME. A trading premium may be warranted, purely from the size of TME's user base. China has more than 800 million internet users, with 98% accessing through mobile platforms. This is obviously an issue, as the only way to expand is either international or by increasing paying subscribers.
Obstacle for Paying Subscribers Although the company's MAUs are by far the highest in the industry, paying subscribers total less than 30 million. Spotify ( SPOT ), for example, boasts more than 80 million paid subscribers on a fraction of the MAU base.
As mentioned earlier, the paying ratio for China was less than 5% as of 2017. This is because of the monetization style that most platforms adopt: a free service with ads or a paid service sans ads. According to a study by WARC , more than 70% of Chinese consumers are actually interested in personalized advertisements, compared to 51% globally. This attitude is opposite from what we see in western cultures and explains why there is a higher paying ratio in the US compared to China.
Chinese consumers actually enjoy seeing ads come across that are tailored to their preferences, and view them as a status symbol. This produces a societal obstacle for TME that may be slow and difficult to counteract. So, while the market may increase, paying subscribers will most likely not increase at close to the same rate.
Valuation TME is already trading at much higher P/S multiples compared to western counterparts Pandora ( P ) and Spotify, but the main difference is that TME has earnings.
P SPOT TME P/S 1.42x 3.63x 8.52x P/E - - 45.10x P/CF - 61.74x 42.43x P/B 42.87x 11.19x 4.29x This makes the valuation a little tricky for TME. Do we emphasize P/S like conventional streaming companies, as it is not an expectation to have earnings? Or, do we focus on the P/E like a more cyclical company? Either way you look at it, the company still seems overvalued based on current conditions. The Chinese economy is slowing, MAUs are nearing a peak (sans international expansion), and the number of paying subscribers is very low compared to that of competitors.
Conclusion It is very difficult to determine a valid way to value TME, as it is an unconventional competitor within the industry. Streamers are not expected to generate earnings. Apple Music ( AAPL ), for example, was created in order to garner market share and promote the company's other product lines. However, TME is generating earnings with an 18% net margin - extremely healthy for the industry. The issue is that MAUs need to be converted into paying subs, and this is going to be a major challenge for the company. Along with this is a slowdown in the economy, which may impact consumer spending on luxuries such as music streaming.
